component.name: file-watch
component.title: File Watch
component.description: Receive an event when a file or directory is created, modified or deleted in a directory of the file system.
component.label: file

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

useFileHashing.description: Whether to hash the files with the fileHasher to drop duplicate events, as some platforms and JDKs report a change more than once. If false, no file is hashed, and the route can receive the same event more than once.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

concurrentConsumers.label: advanced
concurrentConsumers.description: The number of threads that take the events from the queue and route them. Increase it when the route is slower than the events arrive. With more than one thread, the events can be routed in another order than they occurred.

fileHasher.label: advanced
fileHasher.description: The io.methvin.watcher.hashing.FileHasher that hashes each file to drop duplicate events, such as a MODIFY event of a file whose hash did not change. The default #murmur3FFileHasher hashes the content, and so reads every file in the directory tree in full when the consumer starts; #lastModifiedTimeFileHasher uses the last modified time instead, which suits large files. Not used when useFileHashing is false.

pollThreads.label: advanced
pollThreads.description: The number of threads that read the events from the watch service of the directory and put them in the queue. Increase it when the log warns that an OVERFLOW occurred, which means that the file system dropped events. All the threads read the same watch service, and each one registers the watched directories again when the consumer starts (and hashes their files again when useFileHashing is enabled), so on a large tree a higher value makes the start slower. More threads can only help when the events come from several directories at the same time, as the events of one directory are read by one thread at a time.

queueSize.label: advanced
queueSize.description: The maximum number of events in the queue between the pollThreads threads and the concurrentConsumers threads. When the queue is full, new events are dropped and a warning is logged once. A value of 0 or less means no limit.

CamelFileEventType.description: The type of the event: CREATE, MODIFY or DELETE.

CamelFileNameOnly.description: Only the file name (the name with no leading paths).

CamelFileAbsolute.description: Always true, as the CamelFileAbsolutePath and CamelFilePath headers hold an absolute path.

CamelFileAbsolutePath.description: The absolute path of the file or directory of the event, normalized and with / as separator.

CamelFilePath.description: The absolute path of the file or directory of the event, the same value as the CamelFileAbsolutePath header.

CamelFileName.description: The path of the file or directory of the event relative to the directory of the path option, with / as separator.

CamelFileRelativePath.description: The path relative to the directory of the path option, the same value as the CamelFileName header.

CamelFileNameConsumed.description: The path relative to the directory of the path option, the same value as the CamelFileName header.

CamelFileParent.description: The absolute path of the directory that holds the file or directory of the event, with / as separator.

CamelFileLastModified.description: The last modified time of the file or directory, in milliseconds since the epoch. Not set when the file no longer exists, such as for a DELETE event.

CamelMessageTimestamp.description: The time the consumer received the event, in milliseconds since the epoch.

consumerOut.description: The java.io.File of the file or directory of the event, also for DELETE, with the event in the CamelFileEventType header. The consumer does not read it: it converts to text, bytes or a stream by reading the file, which fails after a DELETE

path.description: The directory to watch, as an absolute path or a path relative to the working directory of the JVM. The consumer fails to start when the path is not a directory, or when it does not exist and autoCreate is false.

antInclude.description: An Ant-style pattern, such as **/*.txt, that the path of the file or directory relative to the path option must match, with / as separator and no leading /. The events of the paths that do not match are dropped, and an empty pattern matches all paths.

autoCreate.description: Whether the consumer creates the directory, and its missing parent directories, when it does not exist at start. If false, the consumer fails to start when the directory does not exist.

events.description: The types of the events to receive, as a comma-separated list of CREATE, MODIFY and DELETE, in any case and with or without spaces around the values. An unknown value fails the start of the consumer. The events of the other types are dropped.

recursive.description: Whether to receive the events of the files and directories in all subdirectories, including the subdirectories created later. If false, only the events of the entries directly in the directory are received, and the files of the subdirectories are not hashed. The subdirectories are not watched either, except where the watch service always watches the whole directory tree, such as on macOS.

useFileHashing.description: Whether to hash the files with the fileHasher to drop duplicate events, as some platforms and JDKs report a change more than once. If false, no file is hashed, and the route can receive the same event more than once.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.
